reference_sql:
SELECT promo_id, promo_code, discount_pct
FROM promotions
WHERE discount_pct > (SELECT AVG(discount_pct) FROM promotions)
alternatives:
SELECT pr.promo_id, pr.promo_code, pr.discount_pct
FROM promotions pr
JOIN (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(discount_pct) AS avg_pct
  FROM promotions
) AS a ON pr.discount_pct > a.avg_pct

WITH avg_discount AS (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(discount_pct) AS avg_pct
  FROM promotions
)
SELECT pr.promo_id, pr.promo_code, pr.discount_pct
FROM promotions pr
CROSS JOIN avg_discount a
WHERE pr.discount_pct > a.avg_pct

other_way.sql:
WITH avg_discount AS (
  -- one row in total
  SELECT AVG(discount_pct) AS avg_pct
  FROM promotions
)
SELECT pr.promo_id, pr.promo_code, pr.discount_pct
FROM promotions pr
CROSS JOIN avg_discount a
WHERE pr.discount_pct > a.avg_pct
other_way.tradeoff: Naming the average in a WITH step and joining it works, but a subquery in WHERE is shorter for a single number.
